title: The NDIS Roster Looks Full. The Travel Between Visits Is Where the Margin Goes.
linkedin:
A support worker's roster says six hours in the field today. Full day, right?

Not necessarily. For NDIS and disability support providers, a roster full of scheduled visits and a profitable day are not the same claim, and the gap between them sits somewhere most monthly reporting never looks: the time spent driving between one participant and the next.

The NDIS Price Guide allows providers to claim a portion of travel time and vehicle cost against some support items, but the claimable amount is capped and rarely covers the real cost of moving a worker from one home to the next. For outreach and community-based psychosocial supports especially, where visits are shorter and more frequent, travel can eat a meaningful share of a worker's day without touching a single billable line.

A worker rostered for six hours might deliver four and a half billable hours. Multiply that gap across a team of ten or fifteen, and it stops being a rounding error.

Providers covering outer-Brisbane, regional Queensland or the outer suburbs of Sydney and Melbourne feel this hardest, because participant density is lower and the distance between visits stretches out. A roster built around availability rather than geography can show identical hours delivered to one built with location in mind, while producing a very different margin at month end.

The fix starts with treating the roster as a margin report, not just a schedule, mapping billable, travel and admin time against where each visit actually happens.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

Quick one for anyone running an NDIS or disability support business: does your roster actually tell you where the margin is, or just how many hours are booked?

We keep seeing the same pattern. A support worker's day looks completely full, but a chunk of it is travel between visits that is only partly claimable under the price guide. The providers covering the widest geographic spread (outer-Brisbane, regional Queensland, outer Sydney and Melbourne) feel it the most.

A full roster and a profitable one are not always the same thing. Has anyone actually mapped travel time against billable hours in their business, or is it still a gut feel?

A pattern we are seeing often with NDIS and disability support providers across Brisbane, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria: a fully rostered week of support visits does not always translate into a profitable one.

Today is World Mental Health Day, and a lot of the community support work behind mental health care, home visits, outreach sessions and psychosocial recovery supports, involves support workers travelling between participants rather than sitting in one clinic all day. The NDIS Price Guide allows a capped claim for travel time and vehicle cost, but it rarely covers the real cost of getting a worker from one visit to the next, particularly for providers covering outer-metropolitan or regional areas where distances are greater.

The effect is simple but easy to miss. A worker can be rostered for a full day and still deliver only a portion of that time as billable support, and across a team that gap adds up to a real difference in margin, even when participant numbers and revenue look steady.

For providers who have grown their participant base without revisiting how the roster is actually built, this is worth a proper look rather than a guess. Read the full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
